stories.headline: Spies, strategies and missed opportunities: How the lessons of 9/11 are still being learnt
stories.summary: Twenty-three years after the 9/11 attacks, intelligence agencies and policymakers continue to implement reforms based on failures in communication and threat assessment that preceded the hijackings. The ongoing debate examines both the security measures adopted in response and their long-term consequences for civil liberties and international relations.

stories.headline: Houthis control key shipping route after gains along Yemen’s Red Sea coast
stories.summary: Houthi forces have secured control of strategic positions along Yemen's Red Sea coast, including a key port and island that sit on major global shipping lanes for oil and commercial cargo. The group's territorial gains intensify the ongoing conflict and give them leverage over one of the world's most critical maritime routes.

stories.headline: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons
stories.summary: Anthropic identified and blocked attempts by users to leverage its AI systems for developing biological weapons, demonstrating the company's monitoring of misuse risks. The incident highlights ongoing tensions between AI accessibility and security, as companies balance providing research tools with preventing their application to dangerous purposes.

stories.headline: As Trump dominates convention, some Republicans quietly ask who comes next
stories.summary: Republican delegates at the party's midterm convention focus heavily on Trump while some members privately consider potential successors, reflecting uncertainty about the party's long-term direction. Vice President J.D. Vance gains prominent visibility at the event, positioning himself as a potential future leader as Republicans prepare for upcoming midterm elections.

stories.headline: BRICS summit: Is the bloc truly challenging a Western-dominated world?
stories.summary: BRICS leaders gather with competing visions for the bloc's future, as India seeks to emphasize practical cooperation while China and Russia push for more explicit counter-Western positioning. The summit reveals underlying tensions within the group over whether to function as a genuine economic alternative or primarily as a geopolitical counterweight to Western influence.

stories.headline: Hong Kong court hands stiff jail sentences to Tiananmen vigil activists
stories.summary: Three organizers of Hong Kong's annual Tiananmen candlelight vigil receive prison sentences of up to seven years under the city's national security law. The convictions mark an escalation in authorities' suppression of commemorations of the 1989 crackdown, an event sensitive to Beijing's government.

stories.headline: Israel says it has destroyed major underground Hezbollah base
stories.summary: Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon have destroyed an underground Hezbollah facility, with the strike powerful enough to register as a seismic tremor in the region. The base was part of a tunnel network that Hezbollah maintains in the border area.

stories.headline: Philippine rescuers board ferry 40 hours after blaze began
stories.summary: Rescue teams have boarded a ferry off the Philippines coast more than a day and a half after a fire erupted, finding charred remains as they search for dozens of missing passengers. The blaze has claimed at least five confirmed deaths, with the final casualty count still uncertain as operations continue.

stories.headline: Russian strikes kill two in Kyiv as Moscow targets capital’s fuel stations
stories.summary: Russian forces used jet-powered drones to strike fuel stations in Kyiv for the first time, resulting in two deaths as part of a broader targeting of the capital's energy infrastructure. The attack reflects an expanded strategy to disrupt civilian supply lines and services in Ukraine's largest city.

stories.headline: Canada offers air defense support for Ukraine as Zelenskyy visits
stories.summary: Canada commits to providing air defense systems and support to Ukraine during President Zelenskyy's visit, addressing one of Ukraine's most critical military needs against Russian airstrikes. The countries simultaneously sign a 100-year strategic partnership agreement covering defense, energy, and trade cooperation, signaling Canada's long-term commitment to Ukraine's security and post-war reconstruction.
